headline: Town boards advanced preparations for the April 11 Annual Town Meeting, reviewing major warrant articles, school capital projects, and multi-unit housing proposals.
synopsis: Ahead of the April 11 Annual Town Meeting, town boards focused on warrant articles spanning municipal finances, capital requests, and zoning rules. The School Committee approved an informational flyer detailing the $8.8 million Trottier Middle School roof project, while the Advisory Committee recommended four warrant articles and reviewed a draft FY27 operating budget of $71.4 million. The Planning Board and Advisory Committee both reviewed Article 17, which would overhaul industrial park zoning and set strict standards for data centers. Meanwhile, housing discussions advanced as the Affordable Housing Trust reviewed a 60-unit proposal on Southville Road and evaluated a potential land acquisition on Northborough Road.

highlights.title: Trottier Middle School roof project informational flyer approved
highlights.why: The School Committee approved a flyer explaining that Town Meeting voters must authorize the gross cost of $8.8 million for the roof replacement, with state grants expected to lower the net town share to roughly $5.38 million.

highlights.title: Article 17: Industrial Park zoning update and data centers
highlights.why: The proposed bylaw overhauls 40-year-old industrial rules, establishing noise and odor standards while requiring a 1,000-foot setback and a special permit for data centers capped at 50,000 square feet.

highlights.title: Draft Advisory Committee report and FY27 budget review
highlights.why: The committee reviewed its draft Town Meeting report featuring a recommended FY27 operating budget of $71,415,873, representing an estimated 4.64 percent property tax increase for an average single-family home.

highlights.title: 60-unit Southville Road apartment complex proposal
highlights.why: Developer James Venincasa presented plans for a 60-unit MBTA Communities development across two buildings on Southville Road, with the trust exploring potential town subsidies to add affordable units beyond the required six.
highlights.body: Board of Trustees of the Affordable Housing Trust

highlights.title: Town Common rail restoration bid restructuring
highlights.why: After preliminary estimates came in nearly double the authorized budget, the town restructured the railing project into a base bid with two add-alternates before issuing procurement documents.

highlights.title: 154 Turnpike Road lighting violations and shade tree removal
highlights.why: The Planning Board reviewed site non-compliance where outdoor lighting exceeded allowed limits by nearly 80,000 lumens, alongside landscaping shortfalls and an unpermitted shade tree removal requiring a joint hearing with the Tree Warden.
